correctness.rationale: The four-round universal argument enumerates complete atomic one-point extension patterns of every triple: equality, block, three pair completions, or a generic fresh point, which exists in every STS of order >=7. For five rounds, up to move four a GL-isomorphism of binary spans (ambient m>=4), or an affine isomorphism of ternary affine spans (d>=3), preserves all relevant incidences. At move five the only nongeneric choices are at most six pair-completion points; at least fifteen binary nonzero or twenty-seven ternary points ensure a generic option. The depth-five formulas Phi and Psi quantify four distinct cap points then one pair-completion witness per opposite pair: Phi identifies a Pasch configuration (only binary); Psi identifies a cap with no opposite-pair completion identification (only dimensions >=4 binary or >=3 ternary). Independent explicit enumeration of PG3,PG4,AG2,AG3 returned (Phi,Psi)=(1,0),(1,1),(0,0),(0,1). Pavone’s classification supplies exhaustion of additive types; these distinctions prove representative minima. Repeated selected vertices and order-three exception are handled. The finite checks do not establish all-dimensional stabilization on their own.

originality.rationale: Pavone’s 2014 additive STS classification and the projective-versus-affine Pasch contrast are prior work. Barbina–Casanovas study infinite model-theoretic Steiner quasigroups; their generic model completion does not state this four-class finite point-relational depth-five spectrum. General anti-Pasch construction papers address configurations rather than EF depths. A related published rank-four universal STS result is explicitly acknowledged. The two five-quantifier separating bits together with dimension stabilization were not found in the inspected statements; equivalence under a quasigroup-function encoding could change quantifier ranks, so the language boundary is essential.
